aiSummary: Speckled trout, bull redfish, and flounder are all producing well across Choctawhatchee Bay right now, with recent trips out of the area turning up solid numbers and quality fish — including a 40-inch, 26-lb bull red landed locally this past week. Water temps are sitting at 86°F, so the bite is heavily front-loaded: get on the water at or before first light and plan to wrap up before the midday heat locks things down. A 29% storm chance arrives after 4 PM today, so keep an eye on the western sky in the afternoon and have a plan to get off the water well before that window opens.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel that pushes bait through on both tides and concentrates speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum around the pilings year-round. The lee-side pilings are the prime ambush zone on incoming tides, as fish stack up to intercept the baitfish being swept through. Keep in mind this is open, exposed water — it's typically the first spot on the bay to become unfishable when wind picks up or weather builds.
bridge.todaysCall: The full moon spring tide is driving strong tidal movement, and with the high tide having peaked around 4:38 AM, the water will be moving hard off the bridge as it pushes toward the afternoon low at 4:07 PM — that outgoing current through the pilings is your best window. Light WNW winds at 5–10 mph will create some chop on open water but shouldn't make the bridge unfishable early; get there at first light and work the lee-side pilings before the heat index climbs toward 110°F. Water clarity is slightly stained, which favors louder or chartreuse presentations to help fish locate your bait in the current funnel. Plan to be off the water no later than 3:30 PM — the post-4 PM storm window and exposed conditions at this location are a bad combination.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, along with trout and flounder near the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek entrance are the prime target, while tree cover keeps temperatures a few degrees cooler than the open bay and provides shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish water and can hold bass alongside smaller redfish.
alaqua.todaysCall: With 86°F water temps pushing fish toward early bites and shaded structure, Alaqua's tree-lined banks and cooler interior make it one of the smarter choices for a mid-summer morning — plan to be fishing the oyster bars at the mouth right around sunrise at 5:58 AM on the tail of that full-moon high tide. The outgoing tide through mid-morning will sweep bait across those bars and concentrate reds and trout in predictable ambush spots; slightly stained water suits the oyster bar bite well, as fish are holding tight to structure rather than roaming. Redfish have been showing strongly across the bay this past week, and Alaqua's resident population should be active early before the heat shuts things down. WNW winds are light enough that this protected bayou will stay calm all morning, and the tree cover gives you a buffer — just clear out well before the post-4 PM storm window.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees lighter pressure than nearby Alaqua and LaGrange, which means less-educated fish and better odds on sight-fishing opportunities. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It's worth noting that Basin Bayou offers less weather protection than LaGrange when conditions deteriorate.
basin.todaysCall: The outgoing tide running through the morning toward the 4:07 PM low is ideal for walking the interior grass flats and sight-fishing reds in the skinny water — full moon spring tides will push fish up onto the flats early and pull them back off as the water drops, so work the edges as water retreats. Get there at or just after sunrise and take advantage of the low-light window before the heat index makes standing on open flats uncomfortable; slightly stained water means polarized sight-fishing will require patience, but the lighter pressure here keeps fish less spooky. Bay-wide redfish action has been strong this past week, and Basin's lightly pressured population is worth targeting. Since this bayou offers less shelter than LaGrange, keep a close watch on the sky after noon and be off the water comfortably ahead of the post-4 PM storm chance.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is the top trout producer in the area, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside the bayou hold black drum and sheepshead, adding variety to the target list. It's also the most protected water on this side of the bay, making it the default choice when weather starts to build.
lagrange.todaysCall: This is one of the strongest all-around picks for today — fish the oyster bars at the mouth right at first light on the outgoing tide, where the full moon spring tide will be pushing water and bait hard across the bars and concentrating trout and reds in classic ambush positions. Slightly stained water is no obstacle here; trout crushing baits on oyster structure in low light is a reliable summer pattern, and bay-wide trout numbers have been solid this past week with quality fish mixed in. As the tide drops toward the 4:07 PM low and the heat builds, transition inside to the deeper holes to pick at black drum and sheepshead out of the direct sun. LaGrange's protected character means you have more flexibility if the afternoon storm threat materializes early — but still plan to wrap up well before 4 PM.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a short tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, making it a convenient and protected option in almost any weather. Incoming tides push baitfish up the creek and concentrate redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges, while the creek mouth is a reliable flounder zone. The upper section transitions toward brackish water and can hold bass alongside smaller reds.
fourmile.todaysCall: With the tide outgoing all morning toward the 4:07 PM low, focus on the bends and grass edges where redfish and trout will be positioned to intercept bait moving back toward the bay — the full moon tidal push will accelerate that drain and bunch fish into predictable ambush spots early. Flounder have been turning up on bay-wide trips this past week, so don't overlook the creek mouth as you work your way out; slightly stained water calls for slower, bottom-oriented presentations. Four Mile is your best bet if afternoon storms push earlier than the 4 PM forecast window — it's the shortest, most protected water on this dashboard and sits right next to the marina if you need to pull the plug quickly. Light WNW winds will be a non-factor inside the creek all day.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide spot and one of the most consistently productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay. Summer mornings are peak time, with trout stacking on grass flats in two to four feet of water during early hours. Spanish mackerel make appearances at the mouth on moving tides, and the bayou sees regular pressure but continues to produce reliably.
hogtown.todaysCall: Summer mornings on Hogtown's grass flats are exactly the pattern guides have been running this past week, and today is a textbook setup — be on the two-to-four-foot grass with topwaters or soft plastics right at sunrise, while the tail of the full moon high tide still has water pushed up and trout stacked. Bay-wide trout reports have been strong, and Hogtown is built for this bite; the slightly stained water may push fish slightly deeper on the flat, so work the lower edges of the grass in 3–4 feet rather than the shallowest areas. Factor in run time from Shipyard Marina when planning your departure — you want to be fishing at 5:58 AM, not motoring there. Clear out well before 4 PM given the storm window, and note that the return run in deteriorating weather on open water adds urgency to an early exit.

rocky.aiNote: Rocky Bayou sits inside Fred Gannon Rocky Bayou State Park near Niceville and is significantly less pressured than bayous closer to the 331 Bridge. Freshwater influence from Rocky Creek makes for excellent flounder fishing, and the glass-calm state park coves are well suited to sight-fishing redfish. Mangrove snapper hold around dock pilings, adding an extra target species that's uncommon elsewhere on this dashboard.
rocky.todaysCall: The light-pressure environment at Rocky Bayou is a genuine advantage on a full moon when fish in busier spots may have seen more offerings — sight-fishing reds in the calm state park coves early in the morning can be exceptional, and the freshwater influence keeping water slightly cooler makes flounder active earlier into the morning than on the open bay. Work the glass-calm coves on foot or by paddle from first light, then hit dock pilings for mangrove snapper as the sun gets higher and shade becomes the fish's priority. At 86°F water temps, the cooler, shaded character of this spot buys you a bit more fishable time than exposed locations. Rocky Bayou is the furthest location from Shipyard Marina, so plan your run accordingly — you'll want to leave early enough to be fishing at sunrise, and you'll need to commit to an earlier departure to safely beat the post-4 PM storm window on the return trip.
